Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：禪師落空否？師曰：不落空。曰：何却不落空？師曰：文字等皆從智惠而生，大用現前，那得落空？法明雖省過，而心猶憤然。又問曰：夫經律論是佛語，讀誦依教奉行，何故不見性？師曰：如狂狗趂塊，師子咬人。法明禮謝，讚嘆而退。傳燈大珠禪師問答五則。源律師問：禪師當談即心是佛，無有是處。且一地菩薩分身百佛世界，二地菩薩增于十倍。禪師試現神通看。師曰：闍梨自己是凡是聖？曰：是凡。師曰：既是

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The lion bites the person is one half of a contrast: the lion turns on the thrower while the hound chases the clod.
EvidenceBody: Case verses and comments pair it with the hunting hound pursuing a lump, distinguishing attention to the acting person from pursuit of the object thrown. Dazhu Huihai uses the same comparison when answering why someone who follows written formulations does not see.
Later raised cases apply the pair as a verdict on who follows the immediate object and who confronts its source.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: An animal-training contrast becomes a compact Chan verdict on whether a respondent chases words and objects or turns on the person producing them.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The entry states the comparison made by the sources; it does not reduce every encounter to a general theory of persons over language.

ComparedThings: its attested grammatical and rhetorical deployments
DifferentThingTest.Reason: Standalone and paired forms retain the lion's same person-directed action.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Lion, person, thrower, dog, clod, and words expose both the clause and its defining contrary.

ModifierControls.Finding: The paired texts explicitly oppose the human thrower to the clod pursued by the hound.

FamilyControls.Finding: The explicit contrary hound action; the two clauses remain independently searchable.
